title: Adaptive telemetry retention & erasure workflow for embeddings telemetry
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Introduce an adaptive retention and user-driven erasure workflow for telemetry produced by embeddings + reranking endpoints. The goal is to limit persistent storage of potentially sensitive vectors and raw inputs while preserving enough diagnostic signal for SLA debugging and model quality regression detection.
background: Telemetry from embed/rerank pipelines currently stores requests and intermediate vectors for 90 days for debugging and analytics. Security and compliance teams flagged this as an unnecessary risk for PII-heavy customers. We need a tiered policy that reduces retention for high-risk inputs, supports subject access/erasure requests, and provides auditable events without blocking critical observability.
proposed_solution: 1) Classify incoming telemetry using a risk scorer (fast heuristic + optional ML model) that tags records as low/medium/high privacy risk. 2) Apply retention windows by risk tier: low=90d, medium=30d, high=7d (configurable per-customer). 3) Persist only hashed provenance metadata for high-risk items; do not store raw text or clear vectors for high risk. 4) Support automated erasure flows: on erasure request, mark and zero-shred any stored vectors and append an immutable audit event referencing the erasure transaction. 5) Implement sampled diagnostic logging: preserve full context for a configurable small sample of high-risk requests for root-cause analysis, gated by role-based access and time-limited keys. 6) Emit standardized audit events for retention policy enforcement, erasure requests, and sampled debug copies. 7) Provide tenant-level knobs in Console to adjust retention tiers, sampling rates, and to trigger manual erasure scans.
tradeoffs:
- Shorter retention reduces forensic capability; mitigated by sampled captures and hashed provenance.
- Risk scorer false positives could purge useful debugging data; configuration and an opt-out for priority customers mitigates this.
- Sampling high-risk requests requires strict access controls to avoid expanding attack surface.
- Extra processing for risk scoring and shredding may add ~3-10ms P95 latency; we will benchmark and optimize with async paths and offload to worker pools.
acceptance_criteria: Risk classifier deployed and returns tier tag for >99% requests within P99 latency budget
Retention tiers enforced by background sweeper with no more than 1% missed deletions in 24h in tests
Erasure flow completes and zeroes vectors within SLA (default 24h) and emits audit event with user, request-id, and tombstone hash
Sampled debug copies are accessible only via Console feature-flag and role-restricted API
Benchmarks show end-to-end P95 latency delta < 10ms for non-sampled requests in production-like load
tasks: Design risk-tagging schema and minimal provenance hash (security review)
Implement lightweight heuristic scorer in runtime (C++) + async ML scorer service (Go) integration
Add retention metadata to telemetry records and build background sweeper job
Implement secure vector shredding (overwrite + logical delete) and audit event writer
Add sampling engine with rate-limited store and role-based access checks
Console: tenant settings UI for retention tiers and sampling controls
Write migration to backfill provenance hashes for existing records where possible
E2E tests: retention sweeper, erasure flow, and access control integration tests
Load test and latency benchmark in staging; iterate performance optimizations
qa_plan: Unit tests for scorer edge cases and tag boundaries
Integration test simulating erasure requests across 3 tenants (opt-in, default, opt-out)
Chaos test: network partition while sweeper runs to ensure idempotent deletes
Pen-test/mini audit to verify that sampled debug artifacts are not retrievable without RBAC
Compliance review: GDPR-style erasure simulation and retention reporting
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind tenant opt-in for first 2 weeks
Enable low-risk retention across all tenants in week 2, medium/high phased in for non-enterprise tenants
Open beta for enterprise customers with per-tenant overrides in week 4
GA: enable by default with conservative tiers (low=90d, med=30d, high=7d) and recommended sampling
Post-GA: add tenant API to request immediate erasure and audit export
monitoring: Metric: fraction of telemetry tagged per risk tier (per-customer)
Metric: erasure requests processed / backlog size / median completion time
Alert: >5% failed sweeper deletions in 1h window
Audit log stream: immutable events for retention-policy changes and erasure transactions
Metric: sampled-debug-access attempts denied by RBAC (should be zero under normal ops)
